audit.whatIsWrong: Sap Magic is called 'passive sustain' and 'passive regeneration' in early, mid, whys[0] and whys[3]. The clause that governs it is never mentioned in either layer, and the content layer never mentions anti-heal at all even though the full layer buys Executioner's Calling on the first back.
audit.why: Riot: 'Maokai's basic attack also heals him and deals additional damage on a moderate cooldown. Each time Maokai casts a spell or is struck by an enemy's spell, this cooldown is REDUCED.' It is not regeneration — it is an empowered attack, and Trundle's own chip accelerates it. Chomp is a flat 3.5s, so a Trundle trading 'once per wave cycle' is personally shortening the heal he is trying to out-damage. That inverts the entry's advice: the answer is Grievous Wounds and bursts, not patient chip.
audit.corrected: Sap Magic is an empowered attack heal whose cooldown falls every time he casts a spell or is struck by one of yours — your chip pays for his sustain. Grievous Wounds, then burst.

audit.whatIsWrong: early says 'Learn his W animation and sidestep', and breakdown.cooldowns contradicts itself inside one string: 'Twisted Advance: Dashes to a target and roots them — lock-on, undodgeable. Dodge or sidestep it.'
audit.why: Twisted Advance is targeted — 'contorts into a mass of moving roots, becoming untargetable and dashing to the target. Upon arrival, he roots the target.' Footwork cannot beat it, so telling the player to learn an animation and sidestep sets them up to eat the root while standing still. The two things that do beat it are spacing outside its 525 range and its 14/13/12/11/10 cooldown. The untargetable clause is also worth knowing on its own: anything Trundle casts at him mid-dash, Subjugate included, has no target to land on.
audit.corrected: Twisted Advance is a targeted 525-range dash, untargetable while it travels, and it cannot be sidestepped. Beat it with spacing and its 14s at rank 1, not with reflexes.
sources: champ-data/_kits/maokai.json (W Twisted Advance, cd 14/13/12/11/10, range 525, dash + untargetable + hardCC)

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown appears anywhere except the word 'cycle'. mid says 'track when his W is down: that is your one extended-trade window per cycle'; spikes[1] says stay out of W range 'when your Subjugate is on cooldown'; Nature's Grasp and Subjugate are compared with no numbers on either.
audit.why: The numbers make all three sentences actionable and one of them favourable. Twisted Advance is 14s at rank 1. Bramble Smash — the knockback that keeps ejecting Trundle from Frozen Domain, which the entry rightly identifies as the core problem — is 7/6.5/6/5.5/5, so it is back roughly twice per Twisted Advance. And Nature's Grasp is 130/110/90 against Subjugate's 120/100/80, so Trundle's ultimate is up first at every rank, which the entry never says.
audit.corrected: Twisted Advance 14s at rank 1, Bramble Smash 7s at rank 1, and Nature's Grasp 130/110/90 against Subjugate 120/100/80 — yours is back first at every rank.
sources: champ-data/_kits/maokai.json (Q cd 7/6.5/6/5.5/5; W cd 14/13/12/11/10; R cd 130/110/90)

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] credits Chomp with an 'AS steal'.
audit.why: Chomp saps Attack Damage and briefly slows; the attack speed in this matchup is Frozen Domain's buff on Trundle. Against a tank Maokai the AD sap is close to a non-event anyway, which makes the correct framing important: the reason to keep biting is the flat 3.5s damage and the attack reset, not a steal that takes something he barely uses.
audit.corrected: Chomp saps Attack Damage on a flat 3.5s with an attack reset. The attack speed belongs to Frozen Domain, on you.

audit.why: The entry's central read is right and worth keeping: Bramble Smash knocks Trundle out of his own Frozen Domain, which erases the movement speed, attack speed and healing amplification the zone provides, and that is the single mechanic deciding the lane. Riot's text confirms the knockback and the zone effect. I only attached its 7s cooldown so the player knows how often the ejection comes.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Trundle five of seven stages (Trundle, Trundle, Trundle, Skill, Trundle, Trundle, Skill) while every why underneath argues the opposite. whys[2], sitting under a stage labelled Trundle, says 'Full kit online for Maokai — W root into Q knockback is a genuine kill threat'. whys[5], also under Trundle, says 'trading into a full HP Maokai with W available is still losing'. whys[3] and whys[4] likewise describe Maokai banking advantage.
audit.why: The packet has this at 50.43% over 117 games — genuinely even — and the prose describes a clear shape: Trundle wins Level 1 on Chomp, Maokai owns Levels 2 through first item on the root-into-knockback pattern plus Sap Magic, and two-plus items swings back to Trundle because his stacked Armor and MR are exactly what Subjugate takes. The chart matches none of that. I have not touched the enums here because there is no mirror audit to align to and the correction spans six of seven values — see questionsForUser.
audit.corrected: Level 1 Trundle; Levels 2 through first item Maokai; two-plus items Trundle. That shape matches the prose and the 50.43% headline.

edits.before: Level 1 is a coin flip — Chomp's AD steal and heal from minion deaths trade with Maokai's passive sustain, and neither of you has a decisive tool yet. Don't overcommit; auto-Chomp him once per wave cycle and respect the fact that he can trade back without spending a cooldown. At level 2, Maokai's W root changes the equation: he can close, root, then Q-knockback you out of your own Frozen Domain, completely negating the healing and movement speed the zone provides. Learn his W animation and sidestep — if he roots you, you lose the trade badly. By level 3 he has his full kit and this is his first genuine kill window; keep the wave near his side of the map so he must walk to you rather than the reverse.
edits.after: Level 1 is a coin flip — Chomp saps his AD every 3.5s and King's Tribute heals you off dying minions, and neither of you has a decisive tool yet. Don't overcommit: Sap Magic heals him on an empowered attack whose cooldown falls each time he casts a spell or is struck by one of yours, so patient chip is paying for his sustain. At level 2 Twisted Advance changes the equation. It is a targeted 525-range dash, untargetable in flight, and it cannot be sidestepped — then he roots you and Bramble Smash knocks you out of your own Frozen Domain. Its 14s at rank 1 is the counterplay, not your footwork. By level 3 he has his full kit and his first kill window.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 5, Maokai's passive regeneration and rank-up saplings make short trades go his way because he erases chip damage faster than you can stack it. Your only profitable trade pattern here is an extended fight inside Frozen Domain where Chomp stacks the AD steal over multiple hits — but Maokai's Q knockback will push you out of your W zone and reset the fight on his terms. Farm efficiently and track when his W is down: that is your one extended-trade window per cycle. At level 6 his Nature's Grasp gives him a kill-anchor, and his tankiness means Subjugate alone does not swing the fight immediately; hold R for when he commits the full pattern and the drain has maximum HP to strip from.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 5, Sap Magic and ranked saplings make short trades his, because he erases chip faster than you stack it — and every spell you land on him shortens that passive's cooldown, so chipping him is self-defeating. Your one profitable pattern is an extended fight inside Frozen Domain, but Bramble Smash on a 7s at rank 1 knocks you out of the zone and resets the fight on his terms. Farm and count Twisted Advance's 14s: that is your extended-trade window. At 6, Nature's Grasp is 130/110/90 against Subjugate's 120/100/80, so yours is back first at every rank — cast it early in his commit so the doubled theft covers the fight, and buy Grievous Wounds before you try.

edits.before: At two items Subjugate finally becomes the matchup-defining tool it is designed to be: Maokai's Heartsteel and tank-item stack means a full R drain strips enormous amounts of armor and MR onto you mid-fight, and your Frozen Domain healing keeps you alive through everything he has left. Seek fights at objectives where Maokai is the frontline — activate Subjugate at the start of any skirmish, not after he has used Nature's Grasp, so the drained resistances count for the entire exchange. In side lanes he is still a wall to crack solo, so prioritize the 5v5 context where your resistance theft actually punishes his build.
edits.after: At two items Subjugate finally becomes the tool it is designed to be: Maokai's Heartsteel and tank stack means R takes a percentage of Health, Armor and MR and doubles the theft across four seconds — his build becomes your build. Seek fights at objectives where he frontlines, and cast R at the start of the skirmish rather than after Nature's Grasp lands. Keep Grievous Wounds on him: Sap Magic heals off an empowered attack whose cooldown drops every time he casts or is hit by a spell. In side lanes he is still a wall, so prioritise the 5v5 where the theft punishes his build.

notes: BIGGEST ADD: Sap Magic's cooldown is reduced every time Maokai casts a spell OR is struck by an enemy's spell. Both layers called it 'passive sustain' and 'passive regeneration', which reads as something you simply out-damage. It is the opposite: a Trundle poking with a 3.5s Chomp is personally accelerating the heal, so the correct pattern is Grievous Wounds plus burst, not patient chip. The content layer never mentioned anti-heal at all even though the full layer already buys Executioner's Calling on the first back — the two layers now agree. CORRECTED: breakdown.cooldowns contradicted itself in a single string — 'lock-on, undodgeable. Dodge or sidestep it.' Twisted Advance is targeted at 525 range and Maokai is untargetable while it travels, so spacing and its 14s cooldown are the counterplay; 'learn his W animation and sidestep' in the content layer was setting the player up to stand still and get rooted. The untargetable window also means a Subjugate cast into his dash has nothing to land on. CORRECTED: whys[0] credited Chomp with an 'AS steal' — it saps Attack Damage, and against a tank that is nearly a non-event, so the reason to keep biting is the flat 3.5s and the attack reset. ADDED NUMBERS: Bramble Smash 7s at rank 1 (it is the ejection from Frozen Domain that decides the lane, and it comes back about twice per Twisted Advance), Twisted Advance 14s, and Nature's Grasp 130/110/90 against Subjugate 120/100/80 — Trundle's ultimate is back first at every rank, which no string said. NOT EDITED (enum): the chart gives Trundle five of seven stages while whys[2] through whys[5] all argue Maokai is ahead in those exact stages; at 50.43% over 117 games the honest shape is Level 1 Trundle, Levels 2 to first item Maokai, two-plus items Trundle. That is six of seven values and there is no maokai__trundle mirror to align with, so I raised it as a question rather than rewriting the chart on prose alone.
